dedupe_keys.name: predictive global power mapping and access estimator workflow

description: This Python workflow prepares and combines global power-grid and electricity-access estimates. Its research team publishes instructions for processing night-time lights, OpenStreetMap infrastructure, population, urban extent, elevation and land-cover inputs, then running model-gridfinder and the companion access-estimator. Outputs include filtered connection targets, predicted network lines, estimated electrified population and low-voltage infrastructure length. Both repositories state the MIT licence and are freely accessible. Spatial and temporal detail follow the chosen inputs, not a fixed simulation step. The documentation provides a global workflow but explicitly excludes or trims several territories and splits large countries for processing. It can build initial network and access scenarios for electrification simulations. A caveat is that these heuristics do not establish engineering feasibility or utility-verified connections. The documented reproduction environment uses Python 3.7 and Ubuntu 18.04 and recommends at least 32 GB memory and 500 GB storage. Compatibility with current dependencies was not tested, and no inputs were downloaded or calculations executed.
